sentence: This project builds human cell models with specific mutations in a gene called MED12 to learn how they cause uterine fibroids.
This project studies how a part of the brain called the insular cortex controls the dislike of ethanol and how long-term drinking changes it.
This project uses artificial intelligence on biopsy images and magnetic resonance imaging to predict which patients with high-risk prostate cancer will develop metastasis.
This project tests how irradiation affects stem cell engraftment when stem cells are transplanted into bone marrow to treat osteogenesis imperfecta.
This project tries to find out what controls sebaceous gland stem cells and whether these glands are needed for healthy skin.
This project studies how cells regulate phase separation of RNA-binding proteins.
This project supports HIV research by bringing researchers together to work on basic, clinical and behavioral studies.
This project tests two ways of reducing trauma caused by cochlear implant surgery and studies how genetic variations relate to hearing.
This project studies how compounds made in nature are imported into Gram-negative bacteria, hoping to help antibiotics work against them.
This project brings together genetics research on mental illnesses and helps share and combine genomics data across large efforts.
This project studies how an enzyme and the compound itaconate it produces protect donor hearts used for transplantation.
This project builds a system of sensors and artificial intelligence that keeps track of health in senior living communities.
This project develops ways to put the operating room black box into use and builds simulation training to reduce errors during surgery.
This project looks for off-target editing by genome editing therapies for three diseases and checks its biological consequences.
This project builds artificial intelligence image tools and protein marker tests to find kidney tissue features that signal later chronic kidney disease.
This project uses engineering, physiology and regenerative medicine to build models and devices for diagnosing and treating pelvic floor disorders.
This project studies how metabolism in melanoma cells lets the cancer spread to the brain.
This project tests whether imaging of tumor metabolism and analysis of circulating tumor cells can show if head and neck cancers respond to cisplatin.
This project tests whether natural killer T cells carrying a receptor aimed at a target on tumor cells can treat lymphoma patients.
This project studies how cancers start and grow through their surroundings and tests ways to treat them, including using the immune system.
